chapter_title_en: Letter of Avtandil to Patman (and the Slaying of the Chachnagir)
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Though inwardly faithful to Tinatin ('When the crow finds a rose, it thinks itself a nightingale', Stanza 1096), Avtandil pragmatically replies to Patman to learn her secrets. When Patman's violent lover, the royal Chachnagir (taster), intrudes and threatens to expose Patman for having sheltered Nestan-Darejan, Avtandil silently slays the Chachnagir and his two guards in his sleep and brings his ring to Patman.

stanzas.english_translation: "Thou hast written to me; I have read thy letter in praise of me. Thou hast anticipated me, but the burning of the fire (of love) afflicts me more than thee. Thou wishest, I too want thy company uninterrupted. Our union is agreed since it is the desire of both."
